blind.description: A rustic stone cooking hearth / fireplace built from large weathered brownish-grey masonry blocks. It features a prominent arched opening lined with red/terracotta brick inside. Inside the hearth sits a dark metal fire grate holding pale ash/logs and a cooking spit or hanging rod with a black hanging pot/cauldron on the left. The back exterior (seen in tile D) is a flat planar red-brick backing framed by the outer stone pillars and mantel structure. Surfaces are continuous, solid, and stylized with hand-painted textures.
blind.from_above: From directly above, it appears as an elongated stepped rectangular structure, showing the stepped chimney cap at the top center, sloped masonry shoulders tapering down to protruding side pillars, and a flat back profile.
blind.height_vs_figure: It stands about 5 feet tall (slightly shorter than the 5 ft 9 in figure) and roughly 6 to 6.5 feet wide across the side pillars.
